output:
To: t-achilles
Replying to: p01
Cc: none
Subject: none

Thanks for the tag Lou. Mel, usual disclaimer that I haven't seen your leg, so this is general only and not a diagnosis. That said, stiff in the morning, sore a few cm up from the heel, warms up on the run then aches later, all after a big jump in k's, is a pretty typical picture for an overloaded Achilles tendon and doesn't sound like a tear.

Rest or push on: neither really. Complete rest doesn't help a tendon much, and neither does ploughing through. Drop the k's back to around where you were before the jump and use this rule for both running and exercises: pain up to about 3/10 while you're loading it is ok, as long as it's settled by the next morning. If you're limping that afternoon or it's worse than usual the next morning, that session was too much, so back it off.

Exercises: heel drops off a step are fine, but heavy slow calf raises have better evidence behind them these days. Think 3 sets of 8 or so, about 3 seconds up and 3 down, every second day, adding weight (backpack, dumbbell) as it gets easy. On the bad days swap to isometric holds: up on your toes, hold 30 to 45 seconds, 4 or 5 times.

Two things I'd leave alone. Hard stretching tends to stir up an irritable Achilles, not calm it down, and cortisone injections near that tendon aren't something I'd recommend. Sounds like you weren't keen on a needle anyway.

One general thing worth knowing: some antibiotics can make tendons more vulnerable for a while, so if you've had a course recently, mention it to whoever looks at you.

If it's not clearly improving in 3 to 4 weeks, see a sports physio. Any good one near Bayswater will do, you just want someone to look at it properly and set the loading for you.

And the red flags: a sudden pop, a feeling like you've been kicked in the back of the leg, or you can't push off on that foot. If any of that happens, stop running, stop the calf work and get it checked urgently that same day, GP or ED. That can be a rupture.
